author: alice
goal: Stop Stripe 429s on the account webhook without adding infrastructure.

decisions.statement: Debounce webhook delivery in-process instead of queueing it.
decisions.rationale: Stripe caps this endpoint at 25 requests per second per account. A Redis-backed queue would also solve it, but it adds a failure mode we have no monitoring for yet — we would be paging on it blind. In-process debounce is uglier and correct.
rejected_alternatives: Redis-backed delivery queue — adds an unmonitored failure mode
Requesting a higher Stripe rate limit — support ticket, weeks of lead time
decisions.expires_when: we move to Stripe API v4, which lifts the per-account cap

landmines.description: debounce_webhook looks like a pointless pass-through wrapper.
landmines.why_it_looks_wrong: No test covers it, no caller depends on its timing, and it reads like a no-op decorator that could be inlined away.
landmines.what_breaks_if_removed: Stripe starts returning 429 under load. Completely silent in dev and in CI — it only appears at production traffic levels.

omissions.what_was_not_done: No unit test for the debounce timing.
omissions.why_not: Reproducing it needs a live rate limit. A mocked-clock test would keep passing while the real behaviour regressed, which is worse than having no test at all.

open_questions: Is the 25 req/s cap per account or per endpoint? Assumed per account.
